title: The Dinner of Atreus
notes: p2.2: 'More stew, brother?' is lettered as a caption box, not a speech bubble. Voiced as Atreus (voice_speech).
p2.4 and p3.2: a classical columned temple sits on the citadel; Mycenae had a palace, not a temple. Narration says 'palace' and does not describe the building. Low priority.
p3.3: the kings wear medieval-style crowns. Cosmetic.
p3.4: a girl at a palace window replaces Glauka on a tower. Narration does not explain her; she reads as a watcher in the house.
p1: all-caps lettering, unlike pages 2 and 3. Cosmetic.

panels.visual: Two brothers, Atreus (dark beard, red cloak) and Thyestes (thinner, grey-streaked), glaring at each other across the throne of Mycenae, lightning between their eyes
panels.caption: Atreus and Thyestes hated each other. Both wanted to be king of Mycenae.
panels.narr: Two brothers, one throne. Atreus and Thyestes both wanted to be king of Mycenae. In the end Atreus won, and threw his brother out.

panels.visual: Close-up of Atreus smirking with one eyebrow raised, offering a hand in false friendship
panels.caption: Atreus pretended to make peace.
panels.narr: Then Atreus found out that Thyestes had stolen his wife as well. So Atreus pretended to make peace. He smiled. Never trust that smile.

voice_speech.speaker: Atreus
voice_speech.text: Brother! Come home. All is forgiven. Let us feast.

panels.visual: A long banquet hall with torches, a laden table, Thyestes hesitant at the door, servants hurrying
panels.caption: He invited Thyestes to a feast.
panels.narr: He invited Thyestes to a feast. Thyestes came home in rags and stood in the doorway a long time. Then he smelled the cooking, and came in.

panels.visual: A big pot of stew steaming, ladle, and Atreus' sinister shadow looming over it
panels.caption: He served him a stew.
panels.narr: Atreus served him a stew. He had cooked it himself, for his dear brother. That should have been the first clue.

panels.visual: Thyestes eating happily, spoon to his mouth, with a bowl of stew; Atreus watching with a wicked grin in the background
panels.caption: Thyestes ate.
panels.narr: Thyestes ate. Years on the road had made him hungry. He ate every spoonful, and Atreus watched every one.

panels.visual: Low dramatic angle across the table: Atreus lifts the lid off a silver platter towards Thyestes; we do NOT see what is on the platter: a white starburst of light and ink spikes hides it
panels.caption: More stew, brother?

panels.visual: Thyestes' face in the foreground frozen in horror, tiny pupils, sweat drops flying, silver spoon dropping
panels.caption: The stew was made from Thyestes' own sons.
panels.narr: On the platter were the heads and hands of Thyestes' sons. Now he knew what the stew was made from.

panels.visual: The sun in the sky above the Bronze Age citadel of Mycenae has a horrified manga face, hands on cheeks, its rays bending backwards; below, the rough boulder walls and the flat-roofed palace hall
panels.caption: The sun was so horrified that it turned back in the sky.
panels.narr: Even the sun couldn't watch. It was so horrified that it turned round in the sky, and went back the way it had come.

panels.visual: Thyestes on his feet, arm raised, pointing at Atreus with fury, his cloak swirling, black ink spikes
panels.caption: Thyestes cursed the whole family.
panels.narr: Thyestes had one weapon left. He cursed the family, every one of them.

voice_speech.speaker: Thyestes
voice_speech.text: A curse on your house! On your sons, and their sons!

panels.visual: A dark cloud of curse like a snake coiling over the Bronze Age palace citadel of Mycenae (rough boulder walls, flat-roofed palace hall) in a stormy sky
panels.caption: That curse did not stop with him.
panels.narr: That curse did not stop with him. Greek curses don't wear off. They wait, coiled over the palace like a snake.

panels.visual: A line of silhouettes of kings through the generations from father to son to son, each with a dark thread connecting them to the next
panels.caption: It ran down through the generations, from father to son to son.
panels.narr: It ran down through the generations, from father to son to son. Atreus had a son called Agamemnon. Keep an eye on that name. That curse is coming for him next.

panels.visual: The Lion Gate at night under a black sky with a faint red glow, Glauka watching from a tower
panels.caption: The house of Atreus was cursed.
panels.narr: The house of Atreus was cursed. That's a myth: a story the Greeks told, not a thing that happened. But the palace was real, up the hill. Climb and find it.
